chunk_findings.detail: The report’s own numbers are arithmetically inconsistent. Line 18 says all-test recall is 0.706, line 19 says routable-test recall is 0.856 after setting aside subprocess-driven tests, line 23 says there are 22 subprocess-blind missed tests, and line 29-31 says the remaining misses are “about 20” routable tests. If there are 22 subprocess misses and about 20 route misses, total missed co-changed tests are about 42, implying total co-changed tests of about 42 / (1 - 0.706) ≈ 143. If the 22 subprocess-driven tests are excluded from the routable denominator, the routable denominator is at most about 121, so routable recall with 20 missed routable tests is at most (121 - 20) / 121 ≈ 0.835, not the reported 0.856. With the reported 0.856 routable recall and 22 subprocess-blind misses, the number of route-missed tests would have to be about 15, not “about 20”. This makes the probe result and the decision based on it unreliable.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/test-impact.md:29

chunk_findings.detail: `hub_narrow_share` can raise on a non-empty `hub_rows()` list. It returns early only when `hubs` itself is empty, then calls `statistics.median(r.narrow_selected / r.suite for r in hubs if r.suite)`. If every hub row has `suite == 0`, the generator is empty and `statistics.median` raises `ValueError`/`StatisticsError` (“no median for empty data”), so `report()` crashes. A concrete input is `Probe([MergeRow(sha="a", source=1, suite=0, selected=0, full=True, unrouted=False, narrow_selected=0, narrow_held=0)])`: `hub_rows()` returns the row, the `if not hubs` guard passes, the `if r.suite` filter removes it, and `report()` fails instead of returning a share.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:Probe.hub_narrow_share

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture repository tests run `git commit`, `git merge`, etc. through `_g` with the inherited environment and no isolation from the user’s global git configuration. For example, on a developer machine whose global `[REDACTED:path]` contains `[commit] gpgsign = true` and no GPG agent/key, `make_repo` fails in `_g(..., "commit", "-q", "-m", "base")` with `CalledProcessError`, causing every test that uses `make_repo` to error. Passing `HOME=tmp_path` or explicit `-c commit.gpgsign=false`/`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` overrides would make the fixture hermetic.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:_g/make_repo

chunk_findings.detail: `replay_one` calls `T.select(...)` without catching exceptions. If `T.select` raises an exception on a malformed or unexpected merge commit in the repo history (such as a merge where files cannot be parsed or identifiers fail to extract), the worker process crashes with an unhandled exception rather than returning `None` or being handled, causing `probe()` (via `ProcessPoolExecutor.map`) to raise the exception and abort the entire replay.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:171

chunk_findings.detail: `fallback_rate` and `hub_rows` treat every `full` row as a hub, but `MergeRow.full` is defined as any whole-suite answer ("hub or test infrastructure"), and `replay_one` sets `narrow_*` for every such row after only forcing `hub_importers=0`. A merge that flips `sel.full` because test infrastructure changed (not because of hub importers) is counted in "hub-fallback rate", and the counterfactual still ignores `narrow.full`: it records `len(narrow.tests)` / membership in that list. If that call stays full and leaves `tests` empty or partial, `hub_narrow_recall` reports those co-changed tests as missed and `hub_narrow_share` is not a hub-only figure, so the TS-impact-select numbers are wrong for any window that mixes infrastructure full-suite answers with real hubs.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:83

chunk_findings.detail: The report’s recall figures and its split of missed tests are arithmetically inconsistent. Let `T` be the total number of co-changed tests and `R` the number of missed routable tests. With 22 subprocess-blind misses, all-test recall `0.706` implies `(22 + R) / T = 0.294`, while routable recall `0.856` implies `R / (T - 22) = 0.144`. Those two equations are satisfied by `R = 15` and `T = 126`, not by “about 20” route misses. If `R` were 20, the all-test recall would imply `T ≈ 143`, giving routable recall `1 - 20 / 121 ≈ 0.834`, below the reported `0.856` and below the report’s own `0.85` falsifier floor. Thus the stated numbers cannot all be true, and the `CONFIRMED` verdict rests on inconsistent arithmetic.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/test-impact.md:29

chunk_findings.detail: `replay_one` does not catch exceptions from `_changed_sets`, `_extract`, `_stand_ins`, or `T.select`, and `probe` materializes `ProcessPoolExecutor.map` results. Therefore, if any one merge in the intended 100-merge replay causes an exception (for example `T.select` raises or returns an unexpected object, or git archive/tar extraction fails), that exception propagates through `list(pool.map(...))` and aborts the whole replay, producing no report instead of recording/skipping that merge.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:replay_one/probe

chunk_findings.detail: `Probe.fallback_rate` counts every row with `full=True`, including whole-suite answers caused by changed test infrastructure, but `report()` labels that number “hub-fallback rate” and the re-scoped acceptance asks for a hub-fallback rate. `replay_one` only sets `row.hub` when `sel.full` starts with “a hub module changed”, so a non-hub whole-suite answer has `hub=False` yet still increments `fallback_rate`; the new test `test_a_non_hub_whole_suite_answer_is_not_a_hub_row` explicitly asserts `fallback_rate == 1.0` for such a row. The reported hub-fallback rate is therefore inflated by non-hub full-suite fallbacks.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:Probe.fallback_rate/report

chunk_findings.detail: `replay_one` returns `None` when a merge changes no source files, but `probe` filters `[r for r in rows if r is not None]` without handling `shas` that yield `None`. If all selected merges in `shas` change no source files, `probe` returns a `Probe` with an empty `rows` list. In this case, `Probe.median_share`, `Probe.fallback_rate`, `Probe.unrouted_rate`, and `Probe.hub_narrow_share` return `0.0`, but `Probe.recall`, `Probe.routable_recall`, and `Probe.hub_narrow_recall` divide by `total = sum(r.co for r in self.scored)` (which is `0`) and return `1.0`. A `Probe` with zero valid rows reporting a recall of `1.0` is misleading because no code changes or test hits were actually evaluated.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:166

chunk_findings.detail: The Result table is still arithmetically impossible, so the CONFIRMED verdict and the TS-impact-select gap split are not supported by the numbers written next to them. All-test recall 0.706 with “22 subprocess-blind misses” plus “about 20” routable misses implies about 42 misses and about 143 co-changed tests (42 / 0.294). Routable recall 0.856 on those ~20 route misses implies about 139 routable tests, leaving only about 4 subprocess co-changed tests — fewer than the 22 subprocess misses. Those 22 cannot be a subset of the co-changed set that produced 0.706, so either recall, the miss counts, or both are wrong.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/test-impact.md:18

chunk_findings.detail: `replay_one` still calls `T.select` (and the hub-narrow `T.select`, and both `assert … is not None`) with no handler. The `try` only has a `finally` that deletes the extract. On a merge where `select` raises (unparseable tree, identifier extraction failure, or a `None` selection), the worker dies; `ProcessPoolExecutor.map` in `probe` re-raises and the whole window aborts instead of skipping that sha. A hermetic `_g` and the empty-suite median guard do not cover this path.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:replay_one

chunk_findings.detail: Hub detection was narrowed (`row.hub` only when `sel.full` starts with `"a hub module changed"`, and the counterfactual runs only then), but `fallback_rate` is still `sum(r.full …)` and `report()` labels that figure `hub-fallback rate`. `full` is any whole-suite answer, including test-infrastructure changes. Input: `MergeRow(sha="a", source=1, suite=5, selected=5, full=True, unrouted=False)` with `hub` left false yields `fallback_rate == 1.0` and the string `hub-fallback rate 1.000`, which `test_a_non_hub_whole_suite_answer_is_not_a_hub_row` now locks in. That inflates the rate the re-scoped decision is supposed to use.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:Probe.fallback_rate

chunk_findings.detail: `Probe.report()` prints `self.fallback_rate` as “hub-fallback rate”, but `fallback_rate` at line 84 sums `r.full`, which includes whole-suite answers that are not hub fallbacks (`hub=False`). The existing test `test_a_non_hub_whole_suite_answer_is_not_a_hub_row` constructs a row with `full=True, hub=False`; `hub_rows()` is empty, yet `fallback_rate` is `1.0`, so the report says “hub-fallback rate 1.000”. This inflates the hub-fallback rate required by the re-scoped acceptance whenever a full answer is due to test infrastructure or another non-hub reason.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:115

chunk_findings.detail: `Probe.report` prints `fallback_rate` under the label `hub-fallback rate`, but `fallback_rate` is `sum(r.full) / len(rows)` and `full` is any whole-suite answer (`bool(sel.full) and not sel.neutral`), not `row.hub`. `test_a_non_hub_whole_suite_answer_is_not_a_hub_row` locks this in: a row with `full=True` and `hub` left false still has `fallback_rate == 1.0`. A window of one hub merge and one test-infrastructure full-suite merge therefore reports `hub-fallback rate 1.000` when only half the merges were hubs, which is the figure the re-scoped TS-impact-select verdict is taken from.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:113

chunk_findings.detail: `replay_one` returns `None` whenever `_changed_sets` finds no non-test path, and `probe` drops those merges before recall, median share, and fallback are computed. `__main__` still replays `merge_log` of the last N commits and `report()` calls `len(self.rows)` “merges”. Given 100 merges of which 30 touch only `tests/` (including a `conftest.py` change that makes `select` return a whole-suite answer), the printed rates are over 70 source-touching merges, the infrastructure full-suite case never increments the fallback numerator, and the readout is not the last-100-merge hub-fallback rate the re-scope asks to record.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:163

chunk_findings.detail: The report’s stated counts and recall figures are mutually inconsistent. The table says “about 94 of 138 co-changed tests held,” which is 94/138 = 0.681, not the reported 0.683, and it leaves exactly 44 missed tests. The narrative then says those 44 misses split into “29” subprocess-blind misses and “about 20” route misses; 29 + 20 = 49, not 44. If the 29 subprocess-blind misses and 138 total co-changed tests are taken as true, the routable denominator is 109, and the reported routable recall 0.864 implies about 15 route misses, not about 20. If “about 20” is taken literally, routable recall is about 89/109 = 0.817, below the report’s own 0.85 falsifier floor. Thus the gap split and the CONFIRMED verdict’s attribution of misses to TS-cover-deps versus selector misses are not supported by the numbers written in the report.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/test-impact.md:30

chunk_findings.detail: This live smoke test passes even when the probe fails on every merge in the window. `_safe` converts an exception from `replay_one` into a string, and `probe` puts that string in `Probe.errors`, not in `Probe.rows`. If the newest merge causes `T.select`, `git archive`, or another probe step to raise, `p.rows` is empty and `all(0.0 <= r.share <= 1.0 for r in p.rows)` is vacuously true while `p.errors` is non-empty. A test whose purpose is to exercise the live selector should fail on non-empty `errors` (or on no produced row), otherwise it gives false confidence when the probe is broken.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:test_the_probe_runs_on_this_repository_window

chunk_findings.detail: `_extract` creates `raw = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())` before running `git archive` and extracting the tar. If `git archive` fails (`check=True`), `tarfile.open` fails, `tar.extractall` fails, or the subsequent `git_raw(... ls-tree ...)` fails, the exception propagates to `_safe` without the temporary directory being returned or removed. Input: a merge whose archive extraction fails after the temp directory has been created (for example a corrupted tree or an unsupported tar member); each such merge leaks a temp directory, and a 100-merge replay with repeated failures accumulates them.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:_extract

chunk_findings.detail: The rewritten Result numbers do not partition the misses the verdict uses. Table rows say recall 0.683 on about 94 of 138 co-changed tests (44 misses) and 29 subprocess-blind misses, so routable misses are 44 − 29 = 15 and routable recall is 94/109 ≈ 0.862 (the stated 0.864). The gap sentence then says those 44 misses “split into 29 … and about 20” routable misses. 29 + 20 = 49, not 44, and 20 routable misses on 109 routable tests is recall 89/109 ≈ 0.817, which is under the 0.85 falsifier while 0.864 is not. The CONFIRMED verdict and the TS-impact-select gap split cannot both follow from the figures written next to them.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/test-impact.md:30

chunk_findings.detail: A hub merge whose first `T.select` succeeds is still thrown away if the counterfactual call fails. `replay_one` builds `row`, sets `row.hub`, then calls `T.select(..., hub_importers=0)` and `assert narrow is not None` inside the same `try`. Those exceptions are not handled there; `finally` only deletes the extract, and `_safe` turns the failure into an error string, so `probe` drops the merge. Input: a hub sha where the first selection is a whole-suite hub answer and the second returns `None` or raises. That merge is absent from `rows`, so recall and hub-fallback rate are computed as if it never happened, instead of keeping the primary row.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:replay_one

chunk_findings.detail: The live smoke does not fail when the only merge is a selector error. `probe` records that sha in `errors` and leaves `rows` empty; `all(0.0 <= r.share <= 1.0 for r in p.rows)` is true for an empty list. Input: `merge_log(ROOT)[:1]` is a sha that makes `T.select` raise. The test passes with `errors` length 1 and no row checked.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:test_the_probe_runs_on_this_repository_window

chunk_findings.detail: The result report is arithmetically inconsistent. It says there are 44 missed tests and that those 44 split into 29 subprocess-blind misses and “about 20” routed misses; 29 + 20 is 49, not 44. With the stated 138 co-changed tests and “about 94” held, the missed count is 44, so after removing the 29 subprocess-blind misses only about 15 routed misses remain. If there really were about 20 routed misses, the held count would be about 89 and overall recall would be about 0.645, contradicting the reported 0.683. This makes the reported split of missed tests, and therefore the estimate of what TS-cover-deps would add, wrong.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/test-impact.md:30

chunk_findings.detail: When a hub fallback has no narrower choice (`replay_one` leaves `narrow_selected=None` when `narrow.full` is true), `hub_rows()` drops that row. If the window contains only such merges, `hub_narrow_share()` returns `0.0` and `hub_narrow_recall()` returns `1.0`, so `report()` prints `hub-fallback rate 1.000; hub narrowed share 0.000 at recall 1.000`. That is wrong because there is no narrower hub selection to measure; the report fabricates a perfect narrower choice (0% suite share, 100% recall) instead of reporting the metric as undefined/no-data or showing the denominator.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:108 `Probe.hub_narrow_share` / `Probe.hub_narrow_recall`

chunk_findings.detail: The live smoke test asserts only `all(0.0 <= r.share <= 1.0 for r in p.rows)`, which is vacuously true when `p.rows` is empty. If the newest merge causes the selector to raise, `_safe` catches it, `probe` returns `rows=[]` and `errors=[...]`, and the test still passes as long as `merge_log(ROOT)[:1]` returned a sha. Given a real selector error on the newest merge, this test fails to fail because it does not assert `not p.errors` or otherwise require a scored row.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:385 `test_the_probe_runs_on_this_repository_window`

chunk_findings.detail: The recorded split of missed tests does not add up, so the claim about what TS-cover-deps would add is wrong on its own numbers. The report says recall 0.683 is about 94 of 138 co-changed tests (44 missed), then says those 44 split into 29 subprocess-blind tests and about 20 with a route the selector did not draw. 29 + 20 is 49, not 44; 138 − 29 = 109 routable and 94/109 ≈ 0.862 matches the stated routable recall 0.864 only if the routed misses are 15, not about 20. The decision input therefore overstates selector-gap misses by roughly a third and under-constrains the cover-deps share.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/test-impact.md:30

chunk_findings.detail: `replay_one` still returns `None` when `_changed_sets` finds no non-test path, and `probe` still drops those results before `fallback_rate`, `hub_rate`, and `median_share` (denominators are `len(self.rows)` only). Printing `skipped` does not put them back in the rates. Given 100 merges of which 30 touch only `tests/` (including a `conftest.py` change that makes `select` return a whole-suite answer) and 10 hub fallbacks among the other 70, the script reports `merges 70` and `hub-fallback rate 0.143` instead of 10/100 = 0.100, and that infrastructure full-suite merge never increments `whole-suite rate`. The re-scoped acceptance is those rates over the last 100 merges.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:178

chunk_findings.detail: `__main__` calls `probe(...)` with the default `workers=4`, so `ProcessPoolExecutor` pickles `_safe`. The documented command `python tests/test_testselect_probe.py 100` loads this file as `__main__`. Under the spawn start method the worker cannot import `_safe` (`AttributeError: Can't get attribute '_safe' on module '__main__'`), `pool.map` raises in the parent, and no report is printed. Every unit test passes `workers=1`, so the suite never hits this path.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:414

chunk_findings.detail: `MergeRow.share` returns `1.0` whenever `suite == 0`, including `selected == 0` and `full is False`. `hub_narrow_share` already special-cases an empty suite as 0. A source-only merge in a tree with no test files (or none of the listed test paths present on disk) is scored as selecting the entire suite, so `median_share` moves toward 1.0. `Probe([MergeRow(..., suite=0, selected=0, full=False, ...)]).median_share` is `1.0`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:59

chunk_findings.detail: The gap sentence still cannot be reconciled with the table. The table states “about 94 of 138 co-changed tests held,” which is 94/138 = 0.681, not the reported 0.683, and implies 44 misses. It also reports 29 subprocess-blind misses, so the routable denominator implied by the text is 138 − 29 = 109 and the routable held count is 94, giving routable recall 94/109 = 0.862, not the reported 0.864. The only integer counts that give both reported decimals while preserving 44 misses and 29 subprocess misses are 95 of 139 (95/139 = 0.683 and 95/110 = 0.864), which contradicts the stated “94 of 138.” Thus the report’s counts and recall figures remain mutually inconsistent.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/research/test-impact.md:30

chunk_findings.detail: The live smoke test still passes when the probe did not actually exercise the selector. `_safe` turns any exception from `replay_one` into a string in `Probe.errors`, and `replay_one` returns `None` for a merge that changed no source; both leave `p.rows` empty. The only assertion is `all(0.0 <= r.share <= 1.0 for r in p.rows)`, which is vacuously true for an empty list. For example, on a shallow clone where the newest merge’s first parent is missing, `git diff <sha>^1 <sha>` raises in `_changed_sets`, `_safe` returns an error string, `p.errors` is non-empty, `p.rows` is empty, and the test passes. The same happens if the newest merge is docs/test-only and is counted as skipped. The test should assert that there are no errors and at least one row (or explicitly skip when the window has no source-changing merge).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_testselect_probe.py:test_the_probe_runs_on_this_repository_window

chunk_findings.detail: A valid primary selection is discarded when the optional hub counterfactual fails. After `sel = T.select(...)` succeeds and `row` is built, the code calls `narrow = T.select(..., hub_importers=0)` and `assert narrow is not None` inside the same `try` that `_safe` catches. If the first call reports a hub whole-suite answer and the second call raises or returns `None`, `_safe` returns only an error string, so the merge is absent from `Probe.rows`. A hub merge that should count in `fallback_rate`, `hub_rate`, and primary recall is instead counted only as an error; e.g. if `T.select` with `hub_importers=0` raises for zero importers, every hub merge is dropped. The counterfactual measurement should be wrapped separately so the primary row is retained.

chunk_findings.detail: The reported recall values are not compatible with the counts given beside them. The probe explicitly supports this state (`narrow_selected=0`, `suite>0`), so the test should check `x is not None and x < 1.0` instead of using `or`.

chunk_findings.detail: The previously reported vacuous-perfect-routable-recall defect still holds: `routable_recall` returns `1.0` when `total == 0`, and `total` is zero whenever every scored merge’s co-changed tests are subprocess-blind misses. For the existing `tool` fixture row (or equivalently `MergeRow(sha="t", source=1, suite=1, selected=0, full=False, unrouted=True, co=1, held=0, blind=["tests/test_smoke.py"])`), `self.scored` is non-empty, `total = 1 - len(["tests/test_smoke.py"]) = 0`, and `held = 0`, so the property returns `1.0`. `Probe.report()` then prints `recall 0.000 (routable 1.000)` together with `subprocess-blind misses 1`, i.e. it claims perfect routable recall in a window where the only changed test was missed. An empty routable denominator should be reported as unmeasured (`None`/`n/a`, as `hub_narrow_recall` does), not as a perfect score, because it can make the probe’s output read as if import routes are sufficient when no routable test was actually evaluated.

chunk_findings.detail: `replay_one` returns `None` for every merge with no changed non-test file, and `probe` excludes those rows from the denominators used by `median_share`, `fallback_rate`, `hub_rate`, and `unrouted_rate`. A merge changing only `tests/conftest.py` (or any test file) is not “nothing to select”: the existing selector can select the changed test or answer whole-suite for test infrastructure. In a 100-merge window with 30 test-only merges and 10 hub fallbacks among the remaining 70, the report says `merges 70` and hub-fallback rate `10/70`, and any conftest-only whole-suite fallback is omitted entirely; `test_a_merge_with_no_source_change_is_counted_as_skipped` locks in this wrong denominator by asserting that a test-file-only merge is skipped.

chunk_findings.detail: When the hub row’s optional narrow counterfactual raises, `except Exception` sets `narrow = None` and returns the row without `narrow_selected`, but the exception is not added to `Probe.errors`.
